new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is penultimate by default; in words whose penultimate vowel continues an earlier schwa (now /a/ or an assimilated vowel) stress is final, so that synchronically stress position is lexically contrastive (ba'rat 'heavy' vs 'barat 'west'). Paauw asserts this for all Eastern Indonesia Trade Malay daughters, Banda Malay included, but never states it in the Banda Malay sketch itself.
new_statements.exceptions: Larantuka Malay is excluded (regular penultimate, no phonemic stress). For Banda Malay itself Paauw adds only that it 'has a very different cadence and intonation from Ambon Malay' (p. 60, p. 428) without detail. No Banda minimal pairs are given; the ba'rat/'barat pair is cited for North Moluccan, Manado and Kupang Malay.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical stress, stated diachronically/comparatively for the variety group; no discussion of phrase-level prosody or citation forms for Banda Malay. Caveat from Kaland 2025: for the sister variety Ambonese Malay, instrumental work (Maskikit-Essed & Gussenhoven 2016) found no word stress, so impressionistic stress claims for Ambonic Malay are contested.
new_statements.identity_note: Paauw's Banda Malay data (2007) were collected not in the Banda Islands but in a Christian Banda refugee village on Ambon island (settled 1999); informants said there is no Christian/Muslim difference but this is unstudied. The variety is Adelaar & Prentice's 'Banda Malay II' (post-1621 repopulation), i.e. Glottolog band1353, closely related to Ambon Malay (ambo1250). The stress statement quoted is a GROUP-LEVEL claim for the Eastern Indonesia Trade Malay daughters (Manado, North Moluccan, Ambon, Banda, Kupang, Papua Malay), not a sentence written specifically about Banda Malay.

sources.note: Only descriptive sketch of Banda Malay in existence (App. A.4 pp. 424-447; secs 4.3.1.3, 4.3.2.3). Banda-specific phonology sections give consonant/vowel inventories, no schwa, 'processes similar to North Moluccan Malay', refer to 'final unstressed syllables' / 'non-final stressed syllables', but contain NO explicit sentence on where Banda Malay stress falls. Moluccan, Ambon, Banda, Kupang, Papua) share 'the development of phonemic stress as a result of the loss of the schwa (except in Larantuka Malay)'; mechanism sec. 4.3.…

sources.note: Survey of stress claims for all Trade Malay varieties (sec. 2.1.1, Table 2.1 p. 18). Lists 'Ambonic (Ambonese, Banda)' p. 13 but Banda does not appear in Table 2.1, whose caption states 'For varieties not listed no stress claims have been made' -- i.e. no published stress claim for Banda Malay is known to Kaland. Notes that for the closest sister, Ambonese Malay, Maskikit-Essed & Gussenhoven 2016 found no acoustic evidence of word stress.
